boundary_assessments.assessment: An ExpandedProject raw owner retains a private checkpoint of its actual ProducedProgram/ExpandSession, sealed ParsedSource inputs and scalar materializer. Retrieval occurs only in a closed successful Types->Ct->Expand DB trace. Expanded core, ProducedProgram output and epoch core must share the same strong allocation; target fingerprint, complete Limits and every current SourceUnit byte/ID/path must match. Current aliases/options remain bound by the enclosing full query key. Activation occurs after current phase observer/cancellation replay; subsequent producer/parser/materializer operations still enforce their original actual-input and budget envelopes.

ProjectTypedOwner privately owns the Arc<TypedProgram> and optional TypesEpoch. A produced epoch binds the complete QueryKey and Weak exact Program identity, raw FunctionSession epoch checkpoint and OnceLock publication hint. Disk-restored owners have no epoch; test fault mutation clears it before COW. Whole-frontend and ordinary Types hits activate only after the current closed DB receipt/query is validated. No Verify receipt enters the epoch; current Verify/LIR/native checks remain required.

Producer/Types epochs belong to existing raw owners and are dropped through the existing LRU/prepare/clear lifecycle, without a new independent history map. ParsedSource and entry bodies/memos share immutable owners. FunctionSession epoch_checkpoint additionally keeps immutable ProducerMemo Arc; original transaction checkpoint still clears producer memo/reactive projections. Publication can strongly retain Program, but Program contains no owner/epoch back-reference, so no ownership cycle was introduced. Existing raw capacity bounds owner count, not a zero-cost or strict total byte limit.

checkpoint_for requires the exact previous Program Arc and aligned slots/canonical/binding counts and ordered IDs before it may be attached to that matching Types owner. It contains raw encodings/pack locators and file stamps, no directory FD or verification capability. Alignment does not imply every OnceLock has been filled: quota-limited empty slots can legally serialize fresh next time. Public FunctionProduct digests/Arcs still cannot mint a canonical handle.

The renderer retains a header plus ordered shared Arc<String> fragments produced from exact current item equality. The same ordinary item renderer and header slicing define each fragment. BufWriter streams the full current header/fingerprint and every fragment in order, flushes errors, and avoids the new whole-module aggregate String. Complete sidecar bytes are still written; this is not skipped output I/O. Finite cold/current/local-edit sidecar tests compare actual file bytes to the complete renderer.

Recipe replay is limited to already admitted scalar ordinary O2 LLVM API, no incremental_o2 imports, no closed executable, no resources/closures/post-partition transformations. same_recipe_environment binds all normalized BuildOptions/names/collected/closure fields and the lowering context strong identity, whose complete target/Limits/entry/ABI and ordered source-file headers must remain unchanged. Recipe compares every machine item in order: global/type/declaration changes fall back; changed definitions require exact name/linkage/signature/attrs plus full references, direct-call set and cost equality. The retained actual layout has no imports; changed definitions replace only their owning unit positions, while other current unit items remain shared. Every changed definition must have exactly one canonical consumer. Current full unit preflight and object binding still run.

boundary_assessments.area: Equal object result stops before final link
boundary_assessments.assessment: The final-link key already includes actual ordered object bytes and complete current external discovery. Removing the extra all-object-hit condition allows a freshly compiled object with identical bytes to stop at this actual equal result. It retains object-cache-enabled admission and all key/dependency checks, cancellation and guarded final publication. The native x versus x+0 fixture checks an action-key miss, real O2 emission, same object bytes and reused final ELF; passing it is finite result-equality evidence, not a general optimization parity claim.

boundary_assessments.area: Packed manifest admission and read amplification
boundary_assessments.assessment: The opaque wrapper bounds logical bytes and unique item totals and sorted tables, verifies all sizes/offset ranges/counts and the sum of unique referenced pack payloads before opening any pack. Referenced packs must all be used. Each pack is read at its declared bounded length, checked for pack magic/header, whole-payload hash and length; selected slice hash is checked independently. No per-pack fresh source-byte allowance is granted. The original logical function/v6 manifests and aggregate raw decoder/node/source budgets still execute as consumers.

Only current item locators and their referenced pack records are retained. A historical manifest carries its own locations. Before old pack reads, old unique pack payload plus missing current item bytes is bounded; excess compacts current shared Arc bytes into one new pack without reencoding CFGs. Dirty items use one immutable pack, preserving original ArtifactCache create_new temp, complete writes, sync_all and atomic rename. Final full namespace/plan validation and cancellation precede manifest-last atomic publication. Epoch replacement happens only after final manifest success. Canceled/failed publication may leave an orphan pack, never a partial authorized epoch.

boundary_assessments.area: Integrity stamps, corrupt data and disk hint
boundary_assessments.assessment: A remembered successful complete pack stamp can skip rereading unchanged immutable bytes; first or changed metadata requires whole-pack/slice integrity checking. A hint from a manifest always has stamp=None and cannot authorize skipping that check. The final pub(crate) remember_packed_epoch call is after restored current source_fingerprint/module_id/target equality, and before imported raw candidate handling; it creates only this bounded untrusted locator hint. Concurrent manifest replacement cannot grant Verify authority: current item keys must still match and the pack is rechecked; rejected candidate fallback clears session state. Original independent current Verify remains after decode/rebase.

Both function-v2 and semantic-v6 stores recognize the wrapper and otherwise accept their prior logical manifests/items. New pack roots are explicitly planned cache directories with source/output canonical prefix/inode conflict checks, held directory FD on Linux and original guards elsewhere. All child names are fixed digest basenames and atomic replacement avoids truncating source aliases. Manifest root/key remains the guarded existing destination. Unsupported/missing/corrupt packed input is an optional miss or repair; no raw pack authorizes semantic/native verification.
